Note::repeat¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::repeat(pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t> repeats) const

Copy Complete Patterns Across Dimensions¶

repeat(repeats) constructs a new Note by repeating the receiver’s complete value pattern along each output axis. It changes structure, not cell content. For a vector {"a", "b"}, repeat({2}) produces {"a", "b", "a", "b"}; it does not produce {"a", "a", "b", "b"}. The latter is the job of repeat_interleave.

Do not confuse structural repetition with text multiplication from operators. note * 3 keeps the same shape and repeats bytes inside each cell. note.repeat({3}) triples the axis extent and copies cells.

Shape Calculation¶

repeats supplies one nonnegative copy count per output axis. Its length must be at least the receiver rank and at most three, the maximum Note rank. When it contains more entries than the receiver has axes, conceptual leading axes of extent one are prepended to the receiver.

For output rank r, let padded_shape be the receiver shape left-padded with ones to length r. Then:

output_shape[d] = padded_shape[d] * repeats[d]

Receiver shape

Repeats

Output shape

[2]

{3}

[6]

[2, 2]

{2, 1}

[4, 2]

[2]

{2, 3}

[2, 6]

[]

{2, 3}

[2, 3]

[]

{}

[]

Each product and the final cardinality are checked in signed 64-bit arithmetic before output allocation. A negative count, too few dimensions, rank above three, or overflowing shape rejects.

A zero count makes the corresponding output extent zero. The result remains a defined Note with the calculated shape and receiver dtype, but contains no lanes. Undefined input propagates as undefined before repeat-list validation.

Storage And Cost¶

Every result is an independent Note. For Text and Bytes, repetition allocates new span metadata while all spans continue to reference the receiver’s packed arena; cell bytes are not duplicated. Bool, Int64, and Float64 allocate new aligned contiguous lane storage because their values are stored directly.

The kernel writes destination storage directly from calculated source coordinates. It does not allocate an additional output-sized index array. Runtime and destination storage are O(output.numel()); text payload size does not multiply, but text span metadata does.

Example 1: Repeat A Vector Pattern¶

const auto values = pluss::note::make({"a", "b"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(values.repeat({2})) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["a", "b", "a", "b"]

Example 2: Repeat Complete Matrix Rows¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.repeat({2, 1})) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4, 2], dim=2, numel=8, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b"], 
  ["c", "d"], 
  ["a", "b"], 
  ["c", "d"]
]

The first count repeats the entire two-row block. A count of one leaves the column axis unchanged.

Example 3: Repeat The Column Pattern¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.repeat({1, 2})) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 4], dim=2, numel=8, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "a", "b"], 
  ["c", "d", "c", "d"]
]

Within each row, the complete two-column sequence repeats.

Example 4: Add A Leading Dimension¶

const auto values = pluss::note::make({"a", "b"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(values.repeat({2, 2})) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 4], dim=2, numel=8, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "a", "b"], 
  ["a", "b", "a", "b"]
]

The vector shape [2] is padded to [1, 2], then multiplied by {2, 2}.

Example 5: Scalar Identity And Scalar Expansion¶

const auto scalar = pluss::note::make("x");
std::cout << "identity\n" << pluss::note::print(scalar.repeat({})) << '\n';
std::cout << "matrix\n" << pluss::note::print(scalar.repeat({2, 3})) << '\n';

Output¶

identity
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"x"
matrix
Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["x", "x", "x"], 
  ["x", "x", "x"]
]

An empty repeat list is valid only for a scalar because its length still must not be smaller than the receiver rank.

Example 6: Zero Produces A Defined Empty Shape¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.repeat({0, 2})) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[0, 4], dim=2, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Example 7: Native Dtypes Remain Native¶

std::cout << "Bool\n"
          << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::make({true, false}).repeat({2}))
          << '\n';
std::cout << "Int64\n"
          << pluss::note::print(
                 pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).repeat({2}))
          << '\n';

Output¶

Bool
Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, dtype=Bool)
[true, false, true, false]
Int64
Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, dtype=Int64)
[1, 2, 1, 2]

No formatting to "true", "1", or "2" occurs.

Example 8: Bytes Preserve Raw Encoding¶

const auto raw = pluss::note::bytes(
    std::vector<std::string>{"A", "B"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(raw.repeat({2})) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=bytes)
[b"A", b"B", b"A", b"B"]

Example 9: Undefined Propagates¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "defined=" << pluss::Note::undefined().repeat({2}).defined()
          << '\n';

Output¶

defined=false

Example 10: Invalid Repeat Specifications Reject¶

#include <limits>

const auto vector = pluss::note::make({"a", "b"});
const auto matrix = vector.repeat({2, 1});

try { (void)matrix.repeat({2}); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "too few dimensions: rejected\n"; }
try { (void)vector.repeat({-1}); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "negative: rejected\n"; }
try { (void)vector.repeat({1, 1, 1, 1}); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "rank four: rejected\n"; }
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make("x").repeat(
      {std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max(), 2});
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "overflow: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

too few dimensions: rejected
negative: rejected
rank four: rejected
overflow: rejected

See Also¶

  • repeat_interleave: repeat each lane consecutively along one selected axis.

  • operators: repeat bytes inside each cell with operator*.

  • reshape: relabel existing lanes without copying them.
